prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: kimi-k3.1-pro.
Game: Oxygen Not Included.
About the game: Oxygen Not Included is a real-time colony-management game. Duplicants carry out reachable queued jobs according to native priorities while consuming resources. The standard Survival prepared start uses the base game, Terra and three duplicants at cycle zero. Colony development includes construction, resource production, research and space exploration. The game has native pause and speed controls.
Controls:
Use left click to select objects and interface buttons, right click or Escape to cancel, and hover to inspect tooltips. Drag with the left button to apply an active area tool across multiple tiles. G selects Dig. WASD pans the camera; the wheel zooms. Space toggles native pause and Tab cycles through the three simulation speeds. Tool and menu state can change key behavior.
Select one ordinary mouse or keyboard input from the current screenshot. Pointer locations are supplied by native Box questions; dragging supplies start and end locations. Control names below label functions, not keyboard key names; use the exact keys stated in their descriptions for a control action. For JSON actions, control duration is 0.05..3 seconds, drag duration is 0.1..2 seconds, and wait seconds is 0.1..5. Frozen execution may further cap input duration to its configured step.
Group input:
  left_click: Left-click a visible screen target.
  right_click: Right-click a visible screen target to cancel or use its ordinary context action.
  drag: Hold the left mouse button and drag between two visible locations, including a rectangular tool selection.
  dig: Press g to select the Dig tool.
  cancel: Press Escape to dismiss the current tool or open the pause menu.
  pause: Press space to toggle the native simulation pause.
  camera_up: Press w to move the camera upward.
  camera_left: Press a to move the camera left.
  camera_down: Press s to move the camera downward.
  camera_right: Press d to move the camera right.
  zoom_in: Scroll the mouse wheel up by one step.
  zoom_out: Scroll the mouse wheel down by one step.
  cycle_speed: Press Tab to cycle the native simulation speed through its three settings.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game is paused while you think, then each action uses a nominal 1 s host-time step. Input is released before any integration-specific rendering wait, then the game pauses again. Native simulation time depends on speed, native pause and performance. Rendering waits consume the same wall-clock budget. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.

4. Which game mechanics work in your favour, and which work against you?

answers.hardest_part: Sequencing long research, power, plumbing, and production prerequisite chains through screenshot-only menus while duplicants consume time and resources. The late-game steel, plastic, atmo-suit, and advanced-farming milestones require especially many dependent steps.
answers.likely_failure: A stall in the early-to-mid game from misplaced or inaccessible build orders, incorrect tool or menu state, resource shortages, or too much time spent waiting and navigating. That would leave power and basic research milestones complete but prevent the refined-metal, advanced-research, and late-industrial chains.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Native pause allows safe inspection and queued construction, three-speed simulation accelerates routine work, and duplicants automatically execute reachable jobs. The prepared start has useful resources, while manual generators, batteries, wires, oxygen diffusers, planter boxes, and basic research provide short scoring paths. Several milestones require construction only, without connectivity or operation.
answers.harmful_mechanics: Travel, digging, construction, research, and resource conversion all consume simulation time and compete for duplicant labor. Oxygen, food, and hygiene needs punish delays; technology and material prerequisites gate many buildings; and precise build-menu, drag-placement, camera, and wiring interactions are error-prone from individual screenshots. The wall-clock limit also makes extensive late-game production chains impractical.
